meta.name: LLD / Machine Coding
meta.desc: Model correct, testable behavior for SDE1/2: fundamentals, 15 machine-coding problems and timed mocks. Make invariants and concurrency boundaries explicit.

resources.title: SRP (refactoring.guru book excerpt not free; use article)

fundamentals.title: Singleton (thread-safe variants + why it's often an anti-pattern)
State machines and valid transitions for orders, bookings and vending machines; State pattern
Invariants: consistent balances, no double-booked seats and inaccessible expired entries
Contracts: preconditions, postconditions, validation and error behavior
Dependency injection and testability: separate business logic from storage, clocks, networks and notifications
Concurrency boundaries: identify which operations must be atomic
Extensibility trade-offs: useful interfaces versus unnecessary abstractions; Adapter for integrations

problems.title: Parking lot
problems.note: The canonical opener — do it first, untimed

problems.title: Splitwise (expense sharing)
problems.note: Equal/exact/percent splits; simplify-debt graph as stretch

problems.title: Snake & Ladder
problems.note: Board abstraction, dice strategy, multiple players

problems.title: Elevator system
problems.note: Scheduling strategy is the interview meat

problems.title: LRU cache (then make it thread-safe)
problems.note: Also a LeetCode hard-favorite (dsa module has it)

problems.title: BookMyShow (movie ticket booking)
problems.note: Seat locking / concurrency is the differentiator

problems.title: Chess (move validation)
problems.note: Piece polymorphism; don't build AI, build validation

problems.title: Rate limiter (class-level, in-process)
problems.note: Token bucket + sliding window as pluggable strategies; no good single reference — build from HLD concept + Strategy pattern

problems.title: Notification service
problems.note: Reference is pub-sub — extend with channels (email/SMS/push), retries, dedupe

problems.title: Task scheduler (cron-like)
problems.note: Reference is task management; for scheduler add priority queue + worker pool

problems.title: In-memory KV store (with TTL, then transactions)
problems.note: No single reference — classic machine-coding ask; levels: get/set → TTL → nested transactions (begin/commit/rollback)
